p.description: Moderate to steep cobble beach. Drift logs, kelp. Developed. Non-potable water at tap. Boat launch (high water only). Hiking trail to whale rubbing beach, viewing platform. Hydrophones.
Cobble; Sand at low water. Dispersed site secondary. Sheltered, undeveloped. Large clear upland area. S aspect. Not much view.

Protected moderate gradient cobble/pebble beach in protected bay. Undeveloped. Gloomy, damp but spacious. 1 tent site in upland second growth forest. More with brushing. Possible beach camping. Season

Steep beach of pebbles, small cobble, gravel in small cove. Open spacious treed site. Heavy use including by guided commercial groups. Small trail leads across neck of land to boulder beach with W asp
Gravel, shell, mud beach. Good protection from SE, fair from W. Tree deadfall blocks much of beach. Sheltered, undeveloped. Camping in 2 clear areas on small headland facing an islet. Frequently used

Firm gravel/cobble beach, some rocks at low tide. Extensive site along old road. Maintained by Namgis First Nation. Adjacent commercial site has more infra, and heavy use by guided groups. Water at cr

Pebble/cobble beach sheltered by peninsula. NE cobbles, some boulders at high water. SE mostly sand. Seasonal creek. Whale viewing. Anchorage. Historic hiking trail to Telegraph Cove. Sheltered forest

High beach. Long carry at low water. Patch of sand at all tide levels. Rocks (boulders?). Camp among drift logs on beach at neaps or on beach grass by creek at higher water levels. Dense vegetation up

Sand at centre beach, cobble, boulders at sides or at mid or high water. Enter bay to E of boomer. Reefs give some protection from E. Strong currents in Wells Passage. Upland site for 2 tents 30 m beh

Protected clam / mud beach with rock outcrop. Approach isthmus from S or from N. N has shorter carry. Good foreshore site possible at Neaps, 2 established upland tent sites. 1 marginal in forest, 1 ex

Rough shallow beach with boulders. Sheltered except from W. Sheltered, undeveloped. Camp in trees. One good site to N of creek. Others possible with brushing. Little beach at high water. Water at cree

Shallow mud beach with boulders. Impractical at lower tide levels. Marginal site. Water at small creek. Undeveloped. Possible site to W of creek or at the head of the bay on solid rock which is dry at
Low gradient beach of mud, sand with many small boulders at low water. S aspect. Protected. Camp on high bench in trees behind large boulder on beach. Beach floods at Springs. Water at seasonal creek
Dispersed site secondary. Minor brushing required in upland forest. Beach camp possible on gravel. Attractive. Trail across isthmus.

White shell beach. Steep wooded 'platform' above. Access from main E beach blocked 2019 by blown down trees. May land on W side of rocky point instead. Camp in forest above. One visible tent pad. Pote
Sand, rock beach. Some boulders. Dispersed site secondary. Camp on rough grass. Likely wet at Springs.

Low gradient mud, mixed rocks beach. Alternative W side bay. Protected from SW. Upland gloomy, damp site with 2 cleared tent pads in salal. W side bay has strip of grassy sand between beach, forest, b
Drying cove. Exposed rock ledges for landing. Dispersed site secondary. Some grassy areas or level rock ledges offer shelter from wind. Attractive. View.

Sheltered sand, pebble beach. Boulders at low water, easy to avoid. Semi-developed. Beach or upland forest sites in rough clearings on W side of bay. One sandy beach site at E end. Pit toilet. Door ne

Pebble, gravel beach, with cobbles, boulders at sides. Moderate gradient. Protected from N, E, SE. Currents to 3 kn in Swanson Passage. Campsite primary. 5 wooden tent pads in upland forest. Pole shed
S landing in semi-enclosed cove has mostly boulder shores. E or W on cobble, small rocks. Trails on peninsula through salal to sites. 4 large wooden tent pads. Grassy areas appear damp. Pole kitchen,

Sheltered gravel beach with scattered angular rocks at low water. Forested sites at E tip, view of water. Attractive. Orca Lodge in nearby cove on Swanson Is. Short trail offers views in all direction
Sheltered sand, gravel, cobble beach in cove. Strong currents. Semi-developed spacious site in forested upland. Attractive. Whale watching. Aka Mossy Knoll.

Moderate gradient cobble beach in sheltered bay, exposed rock shelf at low water. Large area with sheltered tent sites, platforms in forested upland at 3 locations. Attractive, sunny. Views, trails. D

Rock/rubble shelf. Signs of a boat run. Vessel traffic, currents and rough water in Blackney Passage. Semi exposed, part developed. 1 platform, 2 sites on rock,1 site in trees along trail around S end
Cobble beach. Exposed. Fairly steep. Kelp. Camp along beach.
Cobble beach. Exposed. Fairly steep. Kelp. Camp along beach berm.

Shell beach at mid water levels. Rock shelf, muck at very low water. S side of peninsula preferred. Upland semi-developed tent sites on duff in open second growth forest. Additional forest sites appro

Low gradient clam bed of mud at low water. Mixed boulder, cobble, rubble beach of moderate gradient at high water. Evidence of old boat run. Some tent sites might require brushing. Not used much. Hamm
Sand pebble and cobble beach. Dispersed site secondary. Sheltered sites in young forest. May need brushing. Provinial Boat Haven.
Sand, gravel beach. Some boulders at low water. May have surge. Currents in Providence Passage. Passage between Cedar, Midsummer Is dries. Large clear area in gloomy forest. Some sites slope. Open to
Rock/pebble/cobble at mid water levels. Most or all beaches flood at high water, leaving angular bedrock. Boulders present at low water. Potential high water landing beach on S. Attractive small tent

Moderate gravel beach, drift logs at high water, canoe run through large cobble at mid water. Mud, sand at low water. Tent pads. Pit toilet. Cookhouse. Food cache. Might be exclusive commercial in fut
Rock/pebble beach at head of prominent bay. Protected from NW. Rocks offshore. Sheltered, undeveloped. Camp in trees or on beach. Views. Occasional use by commercial groups.
Exposed pebble beach. Day Use. Undeveloped. May be developed as campsite in future. View.
Protected beach at high water, mixed rocks at low water, very low tides impractical. Passage between Leone and Berry Islands dries. Undeveloped level upland sites. Rustic benches. Also possible sites
Low gradient clam bed with bedrock outcrops. Dispersed site secondary. S side has camping on open headland between S end of Leone I, islets.. Pit toilet reported on NW side - area not checked.
Protected pebble beach of moderate gradient. E aspect. Dispersed site secondary. Level upland forest sites.but deadfall makes access awkward. Tent sites could be readily brushed out.

Moderately steep beach. Patches of sand, grass but mainly mixed rocks at low, mid water. Signpost visible from water. 5 developed large double sites. 6 picnic tables. Fire rings. Can be damp, buggy. R
Sheltered shell beach but mostly floods at high water. Dispersed site secondary. Level rock platforms at S end of cove. Some rough potential forest campsites usable if brushed.
Small shell beach or through narrow gap in high rock shelf. Undeveloped. Small sheltered upland site in forest backed by cliff. S aspect. Beach or forest sites. Attractive. Aka Monday Anchorage.
Approach at NW side, NE end. Rock shelf, no beach. Tidal rapid at lagoon entrance, max current 8 kn. Grassy saddle in mid islet with firs at either end. Well protected. Swimming from landing ledges.

Sloping bedrock shelves In sheltered cove. Some sand. Numerous boulders make carrying gear hazardous. Sites In trees on N side of cove head. Popular anchorage. Provincial Boat Haven. Passage at Trivet

Rough rock beach with boat run for low, mid water levels. Float, dock but not close. Well protected. One tent pad. Clear level grass areas upland. Pit toilet near dock. Picnic tables. Attractive. Year

Cobble rock, boulder landing. Strong currents. Channel may dry at low water. Channel to S blocked by logs, stumps. Safest land approach over rough terrain from E. Marginal site in salal. Rough site. S

Bedrock, boulder landing at high water only. Low water landings impractical on awkward boulder shore. Undeveloped. Clear grassy area, sloping rock ledge at SE end of beach. Attractive. Sometimes known

Pebble, shell beach. Sheltered, mouldering toilet, picnic table. Camp in large grass field adjacent to community hall. No water in park. Creek nearby. Post office, accommodation, store. museum. 2 mari

Beach camping for 2 tents on tiny tombolo, if tide less than 4.1 M Alert Bay but driftwood might prevent use. Upland accessible up steep bank with 3 potential rough tent sites, in need of brushing. Re

Dock with float. NW aspect. Adjacent beach landing to SE near creek gives access on cobble, boulder, bedrock at all water levels. Sign visible from water. Developed site in mature trees. Picnic infra.

Developed site. Gravel / pebble beach, exposed. Water at tap or water from culvert above the rec site. Road access could be rough. Parking. View. Logging camp nearby but all buildings have been remove
Wide cobble beach. Some brushing in second growth forest needed. Beach camp possible at neaps.
Cobble beach with some boulders. S aspect. Reef gives some protection from NW. A few upland forest sites with potential for many more. Water at small creek.

Rough pebble/cobble beaches, reefs, kelp, in sheltered cove. Semi-developed camp in forest or small rough beach sites. Beach on NW side might also work. Not used often. Windthrown trees might block si

Cobble beach with some boulders, tricky at high tide. Some protection from NW. Forest very dense behind beach but up rocks on E side is small level point with room for 3 or more tents in upland forest

Informal site primary. White, shallow sand beach. Camp on beach or in forest clearings. JK guide has camp at 50 28.95N 126 01.64W. Some sites are adjacent to logged area further from creek. Water at c

Natural boat run up into a pocket cove that appears usable at all tide levels. Upland behind looks usable for camping as the brush and undergrowth in the trees was not heavy and level ground was visib
Campsite and picnic area. Water available, but not potable due to manganese issues (2022). Registration at RV resort office. Pebble beach. Alternate kayak landing in estuary.
